source.author: ov
source.text: Festa dies Veneris tota celeberrima Cypro venerat, et pandis inductae cornibus aurum conciderant ictae nivea cervice iuvencae, turaque fumabant: cum munere functus ad aras constitit et timide, si di dare cuncta potestis, sit coniunx, opto non ausus eburnea virgo dicere Pygmalion similis mea dixit eburnae.
source.text_original: Festa dies Veneris tota celeberrima Cypro / venerat, et pandis inductae cornibus aurum / conciderant ictae nivea cervice iuvencae, / turaque fumabant: cum munere functus ad aras / constitit et timide, 'si di dare cuncta potestis, / sit coniunx, opto' (non ausus 'eburnea virgo' / dicere) Pygmalion 'similis mea' dixit 'eburnae.'
source.text_english: The feast day of Venus, most widely celebrated throughout Cyprus, had come, and the heifers, struck down, had fallen with their broad-horned heads bowed, their golden necks decked, and incense was smoking, when Pygmalion, having fulfilled his offering, stood at the altars and, timidly, if you can grant everything, let there be a wife, I pray, not daring to say, my ivory maiden, like myself, he said, my ivory one.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: vestris egomet tune vellera templis illa dabo, dabit auratis et cornibus igni colla pater, niveique greges altaria cingent.
reuse.text_original: vestris egomet tune vellera templis / illa dabo, dabit auratis et cornibus igni / colla pater, niveique greges altaria cingent.
reuse.text_english: Shall I myself then give those fleeces to your temples? Their father shall give his neck to the gilded fire, and snowy flocks shall surround the altars.
